items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.summary: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions. OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it. Once the attack had JavaScript execution on ChatGPT, it was trivial to fetch private user data from APIs and exfiltrate it via an image reference. The end result: you could create a ChatGPT share URL which, when visited by another signed-in user, could exfiltrate their private data or take actions on their behalf. items.title: dbreunig/nesformer
items.summary: dbreunig/nesformer Inspired by qwenputer by Divyansh Agrawal, Drew Breunig baked a working emulator for a Nintendo Entertainment System 6502 CPU into the weights of Qwen3.5-4B. You can now play NES ROMs such as Super Mario Bros (very slowly) running inside Qwen! In a comment on Hacker News Drew reveals the Opus 5.5 prompts he used to build this system: Read this article and any relevant source code: https://divagr.com/blog/qwenputer. Then explore if you could emulate the chip and ram in a Nintendo Entertainment System (as people do today with FPGAs in MISTRs) using this technique. If so, what size model would you have to build and if you could use smaller faster ones, could you get it to be at the standard clockspeed. Followed by: I think we should build it! Just for fun. It's okay if it's not fast. We want to be able to have the weights, and a cli to run them that we can point at a ROM. Apparently Opus found and then used this collection of conformance tests for the NES CPU released 15 years ago by Christopher Pow. it.title: TV-Detox: velocizza la vecchia Android TV con l'IA

it.extended_analysis:
Il repository GitHub tv-detox introduce un metodo insolito per ottimizzare l'hardware datato delle smart TV tramite strumenti basati su intelligenza artificiale. L'utente collega la TV al laptop tramite Wi-Fi e impiega assistenti come Claude Code o Codex per eseguire una pulizia del sistema.

en.title: TV-Detox: Speed Up Old Android TVs Using AI Coding Tools
en.summary: The GitHub project tv-detox aims to revitalize slow Android TVs by removing ads and bloatware using coding assistants like Claude Code or Codex. It pairs a tiny, ad-free home screen with automated prompts to clean up the system.
en.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how AI coding agents can be repurposed to maintain consumer hardware, stripping away unwanted ads and performance bloat with simple remote commands.
en.extended_analysis:
The tv-detox repository provides a structured toolkit to remove sponsored rows and heavy interfaces from older Android TVs. By connecting a laptop and the television over the same Wi-Fi network, users can deploy AI tools like Claude Code or Codex to execute system cleanups.

The project supplies a minimal interface replacement focusing purely on installed apps, HDMI inputs, and a clock. Unwanted system apps are disabled rather than deleted, allowing users to reverse changes if needed.

Because modifying system packages carries inherent risks, the documentation explicitly warns that certain devices could encounter startup issues if critical components are disabled incorrectly. It highlights a practical intersection between developer tooling and home hardware customization.
en.context: Modern smart TV interfaces are heavily laden with advertisements and tracking modules, which frequently degrade performance on older hardware over time. Community-driven cleanup methods aim to restore snappy navigation and remove unwanted sponsored clutter.
key_takeaways: Employs Claude Code or Codex to automate TV cleanups.
Replaces heavy manufacturer interfaces with a minimal home screen.
Disables apps safely without permanently deleting system files.
highlights: Open-source repository hosted on GitHub (tv-detox).
Requires USB debugging and local network connection.

it.title: Preferenze di addestramento IA: OpenAI adotta un segnale robots.txt condiviso
it.summary: OpenAI ha annunciato che onorerà un segnale robots.txt condiviso. Questa iniziativa punta ad agevolare i gestori dei siti web nel comunicare le proprie preferenze in merito all'addestramento dell'intelligenza artificiale ai provider partecipanti.
it.why_it_matters: La mossa offre un metodo strutturato per i proprietari di siti web per esprimere le preferenze sull'utilizzo dei propri dati nell'addestramento IA, coinvolgendo provider partecipanti tramite un segnale condiviso.
it.extended_analysis: Con l'annuncio relativo alla gestione delle preferenze di addestramento tramite un segnale robots.txt condiviso, OpenAI cerca di semplificare la comunicazione tra i gestori dei siti web e i provider partecipanti. La descrizione fornita è tuttavia sintetica e non specifica quali provider aderiscano all'iniziativa né i dettagli tecnici completi dell'implementazione.
it.context: La gestione dei dati web per l'addestramento dei modelli di intelligenza artificiale rappresenta un tema centrale di dibattito tra editori, proprietari di siti e aziende tecnologiche.
key_takeaways: OpenAI honorerà un segnale robots.txt condiviso.
L'obiettivo è facilitare la comunicazione delle preferenze di addestramento IA.
L'iniziativa si rivolge ai siti web e ai provider partecipanti.

Coinvolgimento di provider partecipanti.

en.summary: OpenAI is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT with expanded safeguards, earlier interventions, and a new commitment to public safety reporting. These updates aim to address safety concerns surrounding younger demographics and platform usage. The measures outline a structured approach to user protection and institutional transparency.
en.why_it_matters: Enhancing safety protocols for younger users is a critical challenge for widely deployed generative AI systems. By formalizing public safety reporting and earlier interventions, the initiative addresses growing societal expectations regarding platform accountability.
en.extended_analysis:
As generative artificial intelligence becomes deeply integrated into daily communication, safeguarding vulnerable populations like teenagers is a primary operational challenge. OpenAI's latest announcement focuses on reinforcing violence prevention mechanisms within ChatGPT through systematic updates.

The framework introduces expanded safeguards and earlier interventions designed to identify and mitigate potential risks before they escalate. Coupled with a public safety reporting commitment, these steps represent an effort to document platform safety developments transparently.

Evaluating the real-world impact of these safeguards will require ongoing observation of how well the early intervention mechanisms operate at scale. Stakeholders will be watching to see how OpenAI maintains the balance between protective barriers and the utility of the conversational model.
en.context: Public scrutiny regarding the impact of conversational AI on minors has intensified across global markets. Technology companies face increasing demands to implement verifiable safety architectures and transparent reporting standards.
key_takeaways: OpenAI rolled out expanded safeguards and earlier interventions for teens in ChatGPT.
The updates focus specifically on strengthening violence prevention mechanisms.
A new commitment to public safety reporting was introduced alongside the technical changes.
highlights: Expanded safeguards and early intervention systems implemented in ChatGPT.
New public safety reporting commitment established by OpenAI.

es.context: La presión social y regulatoria sobre los proveedores de inteligencia artificial para proteger a los usuarios vulnerables ha impulsado el desarrollo de nuevas normativas internas y estándares de transparencia en la industria tecnológica.
key_takeaways: OpenAI refuerza la prevención de la violencia en ChatGPT con nuevas salvaguardias.

de.title: Community-Sicherheitsbericht und neue Schutzmaßnahmen für Jugendliche
de.summary: OpenAI verstärkt die Gewaltprävention in ChatGPT durch erweiterte Sicherheitsvorkehrungen, frühere Interventionen und eine neue Verpflichtung zur öffentlichen Sicherheitsberichterstattung. Diese Maßnahmen zielen darauf ab, den Schutz jüngerer Nutzer bei der Nutzung von KI-Plattformen zu verbessern. Gleichzeitig wird damit ein strukturierter Ansatz zur Transparenz verfolgt.

Die Einführung früherer Interventionen und formaler Sicherheitsberichte unterstreicht das Engagement für mehr Rechenschaftspflicht im technologischen Sektor.

Im Zuge der weiten Verbreitung von generativer künstlicher Intelligenz rückt die Sicherheit gefährdeter demografischer Gruppen wie Jugendlichen stärker in den Fokus der Entwickler. OpenAI hat auf diese Anforderungen mit aktualisierten Schutzmaßnahmen für ChatGPT reagiert.

de.context: Die gesellschaftliche und regulatorische Aufmerksamkeit bezüglich der Auswirkungen von KI-Systemen auf Minderjährige hat zu höheren Anforderungen an die Transparenz und die Sicherheitsarchitekturen von Technologieunternehmen geführt.
key_takeaways: OpenAI führt erweiterte Sicherheitsvorkehrungen und frühere Interventionen für Jugendliche in ChatGPT ein.
Die Maßnahmen konzentrieren sich gezielt auf die Verbesserung der Gewaltprävention.
Eine neue Verpflichtung zur öffentlichen Sicherheitsberichterstattung wurde etabliert.

it.title: Il fair use e l'intelligenza artificiale: prospettive e dibattiti
it.summary: OpenAI ha condiviso estratti di memorie processuali presentate da creatori, accademici, sostenitori dell'accessibilità ed esperti legali. I documenti evidenziano come il principio del fair use sostenga l'addestramento dell'intelligenza artificiale e l'innovazione tecnologica. L'iniziativa offre una panoramica delle diverse voci che difendono l'utilizzo dei dati protetti nel settore.
it.why_it_matters: Comprendere le argomentazioni legali a favore del fair use è cruciale per analizzare il futuro dello sviluppo dell'intelligenza artificiale. Questi pareri offrono una prospettiva diretta su come vari attori vedano il bilanciamento tra innovazione e diritti.
it.extended_analysis:
La questione del fair use nell'addestramento dei modelli di intelligenza artificiale continua a essere al centro del dibattito legale e pubblico. OpenAI ha pubblicato una selezione di estratti tratti da memorie processuali, mettendo in luce le argomentazioni di diverse categorie di professionisti.

Tra i contributi figurano le posizioni di accademici, creatori di contenuti, esperti di accessibilità ed esperti legali. Ciascun gruppo analizza in che modo l'applicazione del fair use possa favorire la ricerca, lo sviluppo tecnologico e l'accesso inclusivo agli strumenti digitali.

Le implicazioni di questo dibattito toccano direttamente le fondamenta economiche e normative del settore tecnologico. Osservare l'evoluzione di queste posizioni legali permette di comprendere meglio il contesto in cui operano le aziende di intelligenza artificiale e quali potrebbero essere i prossimi sviluppi normativi.
it.context: Il dibattito si inserisce nel contesto delle discussioni legali in corso sull'utilizzo di materiale protetto da copyright per l'addestramento dei sistemi di IA. Le parti coinvolte includono sia i difensori dell'innovazione tecnologica sia i sostenitori dei diritti dei creatori.
key_takeaways: OpenAI ha pubblicato estratti di memorie processuali sul fair use.
Il materiale include prospettive di accademici, creatori e legali.
Le argomentazioni evidenziano il supporto all'innovazione e all'accessibilità.

Each group articulates how fair use principles can enable ongoing research, technological advancement, and broader accessibility within digital tools.

These discussions carry significant implications for the future operational environment of AI developers and rights holders alike. Monitoring how these legal positions evolve helps clarify the regulatory landscape shaping modern technology.

items.title: Building a multiplayer game world with autonomous Fable-class models
items.summary: How I Built the Most AI-Pilled Company in the World Don't be put off by the clickbait headline, this piece by Jacob Sansbury describing how they are building Spawn is a fascinating exploration of the bleeding edge of what's possible with agentic engineering against frontier models. Spawn is a massively multiplayer gaming environment where players can use prompts (to the in-game agent, Savi) to modify the game world. I fired it up on my phone for a few minutes and was able to prompt a castle into existence, then a dragon, then ride the dragon to fly around that castle. By Jacob's telling, Spawn is now being developed autonomously by a swarm of Fable-powered agents costing over $3 million in tokens per month ("we spend 30x payroll on AI tokens"). Our agents change the live code directly and ship to production hourly, so they read every error, bug report and metric themselves. About 60% of our work starts from a production error, a Savi bug report (Savi is the AI you build games with in Spawn), something odd in our logs, or a feature request. Savi files bugs herself. When a user hits one, or Savi hits one in the product, she files it. It goes straight to an agent that decides whether it's a real bug to fix, something we won't fix, or intentional design that needs a decision. Usually it becomes a change, delivered to that user within an hour, with a message in the same chat. This is continuous deployment turned up to 11: A loop this tight only works if it never stops, so we treat an hour without a ship as a SEV-0, our most severe kind of incident. Unshipped changes pile up, and every problem already in production lasts longer. The feedback slows down too. An agent can only keep a few hours of work in its head, so shipping faster than that actually helps it stay coherent. [.

items.summary: In general, LLM performance is incredibly multidimensional. There's no guarantee of a fixed ordering where the model that is best at math is also the model that's best at jokes. Despite that complexity, much of the variation in performance is explained by just a single variable: model size. In general, models that are bigger will (a) be more performant / reliable, (b) cost more per token, and (c) have better recall of esoteric facts. As you note, our models are ordered: Luna < Terra < Sol < Astra [ ... ] These days, version number signifies a few things at once: the order of release, the relationship to other releases, and the magnitude of improvement. So something like 6.1 would indicate it was launched after 5.6, may share some similarities to other 6.1 models in terms of training data / personality (which is why it's not 5.7), and isn't a giant enough leap to merit the headlines and expectations that would come with a 7. — Ted Sanders , explaining OpenAI's model naming conventions Tags: generative-ai , gpt , openai , ai , llms , ted-sanders

items.summary: GitHub Octoverse 2026 I'm at GitHub Universe today (GitHub gave me a free ticket through their "GitHub Stars" program). EVP Jay Parikh just announced this year's Octoverse report, and highlighted these numbers in particular: This is a pretty stark representation of the impact of agentic engineering on GitHub. In 2026, merged pull requests tripled in less than a year to 220 million per month. Commits more than tripled to 7.38 billion per month, with most of that increase in the second half of this year. New repository rate doubled this year, to 30.3 million per month. The report includes new numbers by industry, and breaks out numbers for repositories that involve "interoperability or reverse engineering". The methodology section includes notes about how they did this: Top countries by pushes to public repositories, adjusted by profile location . Pushes from each country were summed across the Octoverse year. To adjust for biases caused by VPN usage, LLM classification was used to extract the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code from the profiles of GitHub users who contributed pushes during this period [...] Industry . Public repositories created 2022 to 2026 were sorted into NAICS sectors by a fine-tuned multilingual embedding model using name, description, topics, and README, from random samples per year. [...] Interoperability . Counts public repositories created each year whose name, description, topics, or README mention interoperability or reverse engineering, or related terms, such as clean room implementation, drop-in replacement, or protocol re-implementation. items.title: GPT-6.1 Terra
items.summary: GPT-6.1 Terra It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement. In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use: We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos. Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it. Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks. OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News: In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select. items.title: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox
items.summary: Research: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs console.log() to standard output and any exceptions to standard error. It's written in Go on top of the glaze library, which provides access to a system browser ("WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows") so it doesn't need to bundle its own browser engine. It reminds me of my own shot-scraper javascript tool, albeit in a much smaller package that doesn't depend on Playwright. I had Claude Opus 5.5 put it through its paces and prepare a research report for me. Here's the prompt I used: Explore https://github.com/tractordev/webframe try running it and put it though its paces, build a few exploratory prototypes, then evaluate it as a potential sandboxing tool and as a tool for scraping web pages using the same patterns encouraged by the "shot-scraper JavaScript" command (see simonw/shot-scraper on GitHub, docs directory) Tags: browsers , go , javascript , jeff-lindsay , shot-scraper

it.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro punta su contesto lungo e pesi aperti
it.summary: Moonshot presenta Kimi K3.1 Pro, un modello open-weight da 3 trilioni di parametri con una finestra di contesto da un milione di token. La variante Highspeed promette una velocità 2–3 volte maggiore; l’azienda annuncia il rilascio dei pesi completi entro il 4 novembre. I benchmark pubblicati sono risultati dichiarati da Moonshot, da confrontare con test indipendenti.
it.why_it_matters: Un modello di queste dimensioni, con pesi destinati alla pubblicazione, può ampliare la sperimentazione su coding e agenti. Il valore pratico dipenderà però da licenza, requisiti hardware e verifiche indipendenti, non solo dai benchmark del produttore.
it.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro è il nuovo modello di punta annunciato da Moonshot AI. La società lo descrive come un sistema open-weight da 3T di parametri, capace di gestire fino a un milione di token di contesto. Accanto alla versione standard arriva K3.1 Pro Highspeed, presentata come 2–3 volte più veloce.

La pagina ufficiale riporta risultati su coding, ricerca finanziaria e attività agentiche, tra cui 65,7% su Terminal-Bench 4.0. Sono valutazioni comunicate dal produttore: per capire quanto siano riproducibili servono pesi, metodologia completa e confronti indipendenti. Moonshot indica il 4 novembre per la pubblicazione dei pesi completi; sarà quello il passaggio decisivo per valutare accessibilità, costi di esecuzione e possibilità di adattamento.
it.context: I modelli open-weight permettono a sviluppatori e organizzazioni di esaminare e distribuire i pesi, entro i termini della licenza. Una finestra di contesto molto ampia è utile per documenti e flussi di lavoro lunghi, ma aumenta anche i requisiti di memoria e calcolo.
key_takeaways: Contesto dichiarato: fino a 1 milione di token.
La variante Highspeed promette 2–3× la velocità.
Pesi completi annunciati entro il 4 novembre; benchmark da verificare indipendentemente.
highlights: Modello open-weight da 3T di parametri, secondo Moonshot.
Disponibile anche una variante Highspeed.

en.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro pushes long context and open weights
en.summary: Moonshot introduces Kimi K3.1 Pro, a 3-trillion-parameter open-weight model with a one-million-token context window. Its Highspeed variant is claimed to run 2–3 times faster, while full weights are scheduled for release by November 4. The published benchmark figures are company-reported results and still need independent scrutiny.
en.why_it_matters: A model of this scale, with weights intended for release, could broaden experimentation in coding and agent workflows. Its practical value will depend on licensing, hardware requirements and independent evaluation—not just the vendor’s benchmarks.
en.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro is the new flagship model announced by Moonshot AI. The company describes it as a 3T-parameter open-weight system with a context window of up to one million tokens. A Highspeed variant is also offered, with a claimed 2–3× speed improvement.

The official post reports results across coding, financial research and agentic tasks, including 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0. These are figures published by the vendor; reproducibility will depend on the released weights, full methodology and independent comparisons. Moonshot says the complete weights are due by November 4. That release will be the real test of accessibility, serving costs and how easily developers can adapt the model.
en.context: Open-weight models let developers and organisations inspect and run model weights, subject to the licence. Very long context can help with large documents and multi-step workflows, but it also raises memory and compute demands.
key_takeaways: Advertised context window: up to one million tokens.
Highspeed is claimed to be 2–3× faster.
Full weights are expected by November 4; benchmarks remain vendor-reported.
highlights: A 3T-parameter open-weight model, according to Moonshot.
A faster Highspeed variant is also announced.
Published performance figures have not been independently validated here.

es.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro apuesta por contexto largo y pesos abiertos
es.summary: Moonshot presenta Kimi K3.1 Pro, un modelo de pesos abiertos de 3 billones de parámetros y una ventana de contexto de un millón de tokens. La variante Highspeed promete ser entre 2 y 3 veces más rápida; la empresa prevé publicar los pesos completos antes del 4 de noviembre. es.why_it_matters: Un modelo de esta escala, con pesos destinados a publicarse, puede ampliar la experimentación en programación y agentes. Su utilidad real dependerá de la licencia, el hardware necesario y las evaluaciones independientes, no solo de los benchmarks de la empresa.
es.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro es el nuevo modelo insignia anunciado por Moonshot AI. La compañía lo describe como un sistema de pesos abiertos de 3T de parámetros, con una ventana de contexto de hasta un millón de tokens. También presenta una variante Highspeed, a la que atribuye una velocidad entre dos y tres veces superior.

La publicación oficial recoge resultados en programación, investigación financiera y tareas con agentes, incluido un 65,7 % en Terminal-Bench 4.0. Son cifras comunicadas por el fabricante: su reproducibilidad dependerá de los pesos publicados, de la metodología completa y de comparaciones independientes. Moonshot anuncia los pesos completos para el 4 de noviembre; ese lanzamiento permitirá evaluar mejor el acceso, el coste de ejecución y la adaptación del modelo.
es.context: Los modelos de pesos abiertos permiten examinar y ejecutar los pesos, siempre dentro de las condiciones de su licencia. Un contexto muy amplio puede ayudar con documentos extensos y procesos de varios pasos, pero también exige más memoria y capacidad de cálculo.
key_takeaways: Contexto anunciado de hasta un millón de tokens.
Highspeed promete entre 2 y 3 veces más velocidad.
Los pesos completos se esperan para el 4 de noviembre; los benchmarks son del fabricante.
highlights: Modelo de pesos abiertos de 3T parámetros, según Moonshot.
Se anuncia una variante Highspeed.

de.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro setzt auf langen Kontext und offene Gewichte
de.summary: Moonshot stellt Kimi K3.1 Pro vor: ein Open-Weight-Modell mit 3 Billionen Parametern und einem Kontextfenster von einer Million Tokens. Die Highspeed-Variante soll zwei- bis dreimal schneller sein; die vollständigen Gewichte sollen bis zum 4. November folgen. Die veröffentlichten Benchmarkwerte stammen vom Anbieter und müssen unabhängig überprüft werden.
de.why_it_matters: Ein Modell dieser Größe mit frei verfügbaren Gewichten könnte Experimente mit Coding und Agenten-Workflows erleichtern. Der praktische Nutzen hängt jedoch von Lizenz, Hardwarebedarf und unabhängigen Tests ab – nicht allein von den Benchmarks des Herstellers.
de.extended_analysis:
Kimi K3.1 Pro ist das neue Spitzenmodell, das Moonshot AI angekündigt hat. Das Unternehmen beschreibt es als Open-Weight-System mit 3 Billionen Parametern und einem Kontextfenster von bis zu einer Million Tokens. Zusätzlich gibt es eine Highspeed-Version, die laut Anbieter zwei- bis dreimal schneller arbeitet.

Der offizielle Beitrag nennt Ergebnisse für Coding, Finanzrecherche und agentische Aufgaben, darunter 65,7 Prozent auf Terminal-Bench 4.0. Diese Zahlen wurden vom Hersteller veröffentlicht; ihre Reproduzierbarkeit hängt von den verfügbaren Gewichten, der vollständigen Methodik und unabhängigen Vergleichen ab. Moonshot stellt die vollständigen Gewichte bis zum 4. November in Aussicht. Erst dann lassen sich Zugänglichkeit, Betriebskosten und Anpassungsmöglichkeiten besser beurteilen.
de.context: Open-Weight-Modelle erlauben Entwicklern und Organisationen, Gewichte im Rahmen der Lizenz zu prüfen und auszuführen. Ein sehr langes Kontextfenster hilft bei großen Dokumenten und mehrstufigen Aufgaben, erhöht aber auch den Speicher- und Rechenbedarf.

Highspeed soll zwei- bis dreimal schneller sein.
Vollständige Gewichte bis 4. November angekündigt; Benchmarks sind Anbieterangaben.
highlights: Laut Moonshot ein Open-Weight-Modell mit 3T Parametern.

items.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
items.summary: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro Kimi K3.1 Pro landed on the Kimi API today - it's not yet open weights, but Moonshot promise "Full model weights will be released by Nov 4, 2026". They're also offering a "Highspeed" version that's 2-3x faster, at twice the price (except for input token cache hits, which are priced the same). The US dollar pricing is $2.00/million tokens for input and $10/million for output - the same as GPT-6.1 Sol and half the price of Claude Opus 5.5. Moonshot's own benchmarks show Kimi as approximately level with Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra - beating them on a few benchmarks, coming close on others. Artificial Analysis scored Kimi at 55 - ahead of Claude Fable 5.1, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon (all at 53) and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 (58). This is the first time a (soon-to-be) open weight model has scored this highly against the frontier. I tried it out via the Moonshot API using the llm openai endpoint command I added to LLM 0.32 back in August: llm openai endpoint \ https://api.moonshot.ai/v1 \ --key kimi \ -m kimi-k3.1-pro \ "Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle" \ --responses \ -o reasoning_effort low \ > kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stdout.txt \ 2> kimi-k3.1-pro-pelican-low.stderr.txt llm openai endpoint can run prompts against any OpenAI-compatible endpoint but doesn't log the results, hence the extra options to save stdout and stderr (the reasoning trace). Here are the pelicans I got for Kimi K3.1 Pro on the three reasoning levels it supports - low, medium, and max. Available in four sizes (5M to 209M parameters), it balances accuracy and efficiency, running efficiently on CPUs and excelling in zero-shot forecasting for diverse domains. The model combines synthetic pre-training, covariate-aware attention, and long-context learning, with fine-tuning options for domain adaptation via Mistral Forge. Today, we’re releasing Timestral, our first family of time-series foundation models. Our largest model, at just 209M parameters, ranks first on all three of the field's main public benchmarks, GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, outperforming the previous state of the art with only two-thirds of the model parameters. Timestral delivers probabilistic, multivariate forecasts and supports past-only and known-future covariates. Our family of models sits on the Pareto front of forecasting accuracy versus model size, delivering leading performance at each size. Results have been submitted to the GIFT-Eval and TIME leaderboards. Time Series Foundation Models (TSFM) Time series is one of the most common data types in enterprise, from sensor telemetry to observability metrics. Forecasts built on it drive decisions in capacity planning, energy, supply chains, risk and maintenance. Industrial plants forecast process sensors against the production schedule, catch equipment drift before it fails, and plan capacity and spare parts across thousands of assets. Finance teams forecast flows, volumes, and volatility to inform positions, hedging, and treasury across thousands of accounts. Classical models such as ARIMA and linear regression remain well-established tools for forecasting time series. These models are usually fitted to a single series and learn only from that series' history. Deep learning models such as PatchTST add the capacity to learn nonlinear patterns across many related series, but they are still typically trained from scratch on each dataset, so what they learn doesn't carry over to new domains. Time series foundation models bring the pre-training approach to time series. Trained on a large and diverse corpus, our model learns patterns that transfer across series, forecasting zero-shot on data it has never seen, even in domains where data is scarce. Benchmark Results We evaluated Timestral on the three main public forecasting benchmarks: GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench. Among pre-trained, zero-shot models, it ranks first across all five metrics. These results come from a single checkpoint, without ensembling. it.title: Timestral: modelli compatti per prevedere dati che cambiano nel tempo
it.summary: Mistral presenta Timestral, una famiglia di modelli per previsioni su serie temporali in quattro dimensioni, da 5 a 209 milioni di parametri. L’azienda dichiara risultati ai vertici di benchmark pubblici e inferenza su CPU: l’obiettivo è rendere più accessibili previsioni probabilistiche e multivariate in ambiti come manutenzione, energia e finanza.
it.why_it_matters: Molte decisioni operative dipendono da dati che evolvono nel tempo. Modelli relativamente piccoli, capaci di stimare più variabili e l’incertezza delle previsioni, potrebbero rendere queste tecniche più praticabili anche fuori dai grandi cluster GPU.
it.extended_analysis:
Timestral è la prima famiglia di foundation model di Mistral dedicata alle serie temporali. La gamma comprende quattro taglie, da 5 a 209 milioni di parametri, e punta su previsioni probabilistiche e multivariate: non un solo valore futuro, ma una distribuzione di scenari e relazioni tra più segnali.

Mistral dichiara il primo posto su GIFT-Eval, TIME e fev-bench per i modelli pre-addestrati valutati in modalità zero-shot. L’azienda indica inoltre tempi di inferenza su CPU standard e l’uso di variabili note in anticipo, come calendari o programmi di produzione. Sono risultati e misure pubblicati dal produttore: per valutarne l’utilità concreta serviranno test sui dati e sui vincoli dei singoli settori.
it.context: Le serie temporali descrivono fenomeni misurati nel tempo: consumi, sensori industriali, domanda, prezzi e metriche operative. Un foundation model pre-addestrato cerca di trasferire schemi appresi da molti dataset a nuove serie, riducendo la necessità di addestrare da zero ogni singolo modello.
key_takeaways: Quattro versioni: 5M, 28M, 123M e 209M parametri.
Previsioni multivariate e probabilistiche, con variabili passate e future note.
Mistral dichiara inferenza su CPU e risultati di benchmark da verificare sui casi d’uso reali.
highlights: Prima famiglia di modelli Timestral di Mistral.
Progettata per forecasting zero-shot su serie nuove.
Il produttore pubblica benchmark e tempi CPU.

en.title: Timestral brings compact foundation models to time-series forecasting
en.summary: Mistral introduces Timestral, a family of time-series forecasting models in four sizes, from 5M to 209M parameters. The company reports leading results on public benchmarks and CPU inference, aiming to make probabilistic, multivariate forecasts more practical for areas such as maintenance, energy and finance.
en.why_it_matters: Operational decisions often depend on signals that change over time. Relatively small models that estimate multiple variables and forecast uncertainty could make advanced forecasting more accessible beyond GPU-heavy infrastructure.
en.extended_analysis:
Timestral is Mistral’s first family of foundation models designed for time series. It comes in four sizes, from 5M to 209M parameters, and focuses on probabilistic, multivariate forecasts: rather than outputting a single future value, it can estimate a range of outcomes and relationships among signals.

Mistral says the models lead GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among pretrained models evaluated in zero-shot settings. The company also reports CPU inference times and support for known-future inputs such as calendars and production schedules. These are vendor-published claims and measurements; their practical value will need to be tested against the data, latency and reliability requirements of each domain.
en.context: Time series describe measurements over time, including energy use, industrial sensors, demand, prices and operational metrics. A pretrained foundation model aims to transfer patterns learned from many datasets to new series, reducing the need to train a separate model from scratch for every use case.
key_takeaways: Four sizes: 5M, 28M, 123M and 209M parameters.
Probabilistic, multivariate forecasts with past and known-future covariates.
Mistral reports CPU inference and benchmark results that still need real-world validation.
highlights: Mistral’s first Timestral time-series model family.
Designed for zero-shot forecasting on unseen series.
The vendor publishes benchmark results and CPU timings.

es.title: Timestral lleva modelos compactos a la predicción de series temporales
es.summary: Mistral presenta Timestral, una familia de modelos para predecir series temporales en cuatro tamaños, de 5 a 209 millones de parámetros. La empresa afirma lograr resultados destacados en benchmarks públicos y ejecutar inferencias en CPU, con el objetivo de facilitar previsiones probabilísticas y multivariantes en mantenimiento, energía y finanzas.
es.why_it_matters: Muchas decisiones operativas dependen de señales que cambian con el tiempo. Modelos relativamente pequeños capaces de estimar varias variables y la incertidumbre podrían acercar estas técnicas a organizaciones sin grandes infraestructuras GPU.
es.extended_analysis:
Timestral es la primera familia de modelos fundacionales de Mistral dedicada a las series temporales. Incluye cuatro tamaños, de 5 a 209 millones de parámetros, y se centra en previsiones probabilísticas y multivariantes: no ofrece solo un valor futuro, sino un conjunto de escenarios y relaciones entre señales.

Mistral afirma liderar GIFT-Eval, TIME y fev-bench entre los modelos preentrenados evaluados en modo zero-shot. La compañía también publica tiempos de inferencia en CPU y soporte para variables futuras conocidas, como calendarios y planes de producción. Son resultados y mediciones comunicados por el fabricante; su utilidad deberá comprobarse con los datos, la latencia y los requisitos de fiabilidad de cada sector.
es.context: Las series temporales representan mediciones a lo largo del tiempo: consumo energético, sensores industriales, demanda, precios y métricas operativas. Un modelo fundacional preentrenado intenta transferir patrones aprendidos de muchos conjuntos de datos a nuevas series y reducir la necesidad de entrenar un modelo desde cero para cada caso.

zh-CN.title: Timestral：让轻量模型也能进行时间序列预测
zh-CN.summary: Mistral 推出 Timestral 时间序列模型家族，提供 5M 至 209M 参数的四种规格。公司称其在公开基准测试中表现领先，并可在 CPU 上运行，目标是让维护、能源和金融等领域更容易使用概率式、多变量预测。
zh-CN.why_it_matters: 许多运营决策都依赖随时间变化的数据。能够同时预测多个变量并表达不确定性的轻量模型，有望降低高级预测技术对大型 GPU 基础设施的依赖。
zh-CN.extended_analysis:
Timestral 是 Mistral 首个专为时间序列设计的基础模型家族，共有四种规格，参数量从 5M 到 209M。它强调概率式、多变量预测：模型不只给出一个未来数值，还尝试描述可能结果的范围以及不同信号之间的关系。

Mistral 表示，在预训练模型的 zero-shot 评测中，Timestral 在 GIFT-Eval、TIME 和 fev-bench 上取得领先成绩。公司还公布了 CPU 推理速度，并支持日历、生产计划等已知未来变量。这些属于厂商发布的结果和测量，实际效果仍需结合各行业的数据、延迟和可靠性要求进行验证。
zh-CN.context: 时间序列是按时间连续记录的数据，例如能源消耗、工业传感器、需求、价格和运营指标。预训练基础模型希望把从大量数据集中学到的规律迁移到新的序列，减少每个场景都从头训练模型的需求。
key_takeaways: 提供 5M、28M、123M 和 209M 四种规格。
支持概率式、多变量预测及已知未来协变量。
CPU 运行和基准成绩来自厂商公布，仍需真实场景检验。
highlights: Mistral 首个时间序列 Timestral 模型家族。
面向未见过的数据进行 zero-shot 预测。
官方公布了基准成绩和 CPU 推理时间。

de.title: Timestral bringt kompakte Foundation-Modelle in die Zeitreihenprognose
de.summary: Mistral stellt Timestral vor, eine Familie von Zeitreihenmodellen in vier Größen von 5 bis 209 Millionen Parametern. Das Unternehmen meldet Spitzenwerte auf öffentlichen Benchmarks und Inferenz auf CPUs. Damit sollen probabilistische Prognosen über mehrere Variablen etwa in Wartung, Energie und Finanzwesen leichter nutzbar werden.
de.why_it_matters: Viele operative Entscheidungen hängen von Signalen ab, die sich laufend verändern. Relativ kleine Modelle, die mehrere Variablen und die Unsicherheit einer Prognose erfassen, könnten fortgeschrittene Vorhersagen auch ohne große GPU-Infrastruktur praktikabler machen.
de.extended_analysis:
Timestral ist Mistrals erste Foundation-Model-Familie für Zeitreihen. Sie umfasst vier Größen von 5 bis 209 Millionen Parametern und zielt auf probabilistische Prognosen über mehrere Variablen. Statt nur einen zukünftigen Wert auszugeben, soll das Modell mögliche Szenarien und Beziehungen zwischen Signalen abbilden.

Mistral zufolge liegt Timestral bei GIFT-Eval, TIME und fev-bench unter den vortrainierten Zero-Shot-Modellen vorn. Das Unternehmen veröffentlicht außerdem CPU-Laufzeiten und Unterstützung für bekannte zukünftige Eingaben wie Kalender oder Produktionspläne. Diese Ergebnisse und Messwerte stammen vom Anbieter; ihr praktischer Nutzen muss mit den Daten, Latenz- und Zuverlässigkeitsanforderungen der jeweiligen Branche geprüft werden.
de.context: Zeitreihen beschreiben Messwerte im Verlauf der Zeit, etwa Energieverbrauch, Industriesensoren, Nachfrage, Preise und Betriebskennzahlen. Ein vortrainiertes Foundation-Modell soll Muster aus vielen Datensätzen auf neue Reihen übertragen und damit das Training eines separaten Modells für jeden Anwendungsfall verringern.
key_takeaways: Vier Größen: 5M, 28M, 123M und 209M Parameter.
Probabilistische Prognosen über mehrere Variablen mit vergangenen und bekannten zukünftigen Einflussgrößen.
CPU-Laufzeiten und Benchmarkwerte sind Herstellerangaben und müssen im Einsatz geprüft werden.
highlights: Mistrals erste Timestral-Modellfamilie für Zeitreihen.
Für Zero-Shot-Prognosen auf unbekannten Daten ausgelegt.
Der Hersteller veröffentlicht Benchmarks und CPU-Zeiten.

items.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
items.summary: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise This is very, very bad news: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores. Any software that bundles a list of trusted certificates needs to be updated. This site is tracking software updates via this GitHub repository - Linux distros need to update their ca-certificates packages. In Python world uv 0.13.4 and pip 26.2.2 and certifi 2026.10.19 have been released with upgraded certificate lists. There's a very informative thread about this on the official Python forum. items.summary: My obituary for programming Jeremy Scheff poignantly captures the key loss caused by coding agents for career programmers who enjoyed the puzzle of developing code: Programming turned into one of the greatest jobs you could imagine. You got paid to work on tricky little logic puzzles. The trickier the puzzle, the more you got paid. But even pretty simple puzzles were worth a lot of money because regular people just couldn't do it! No, they needed us. They would give us a problem and we would solve it the way we wanted. We set the strategy, we made the timeline, we defined what was and was not possible. If you're a programmer who thrives on building working systems and doesn't care too deeply about the problems solved along the way, LLMs are the gift that keeps on giving. items.title: llm-echo 0.5
items.summary: Release: llm-echo 0.5 I'm working towards a new LLM release, and testing PRs caused me to revisit the llm-echo debug plugin. This plugin provides a "model" which doesn't involve an LLM at all - it just repeats back the prompts that have been fed to it. The new release now updates the simulated token usage counts to take tool calls, system prompts, and reasoning tokens into account. Example usage: uvx --with llm-echo llm -m echo 'hi there' -o thinking 1 --usage Outputs: First I consider the prompt, then I decide what to say. { "prompt": "hi there", "system": "", "attachments": [], "stream": true, "previous": [] } Token usage: 2 input, 24 output Tags: llm

items.title: Your Ranking Model Is Optimizing the Wrong Thing with Zoe Weil - #780
items.summary: In this episode, Zoe Weil, co-founder and CEO of Sequen, joins us to discuss how ranking systems can use live behavioral signals to optimize for purchases rather than clicks or search relevance alone. Zoe explains why approaches developed at data-rich social platforms don’t necessarily translate to retailers and how Sequen uses scroll speed, hover duration, and other in-session interactions to infer shopper intent without relying on user identity. We explore the company’s large event models and its architecture of specialized models that transform streaming events into features for downstream rankers. Zoe describes the infrastructure required to serve dynamic rankings within milliseconds, why the team chose Rust for its backend, and how evaluation harnesses connect model improvements to business outcomes. We also discuss the tradeoffs between advertising and organic revenue, continuous model improvement, and the boundary between useful personalization and surveillance. 🗒️ Full show notes: ⁠⁠https://twimlai.com/go/780.

it.title: Lab-in-the-Loop alla velocità di calcolo con Ian Quigley
it.summary: In questo episodio di Latent Space, Ian Quigley di Leash Bio discute il concetto di Lab-in-the-Loop alla velocità di calcolo. Vengono esplorate le sfide aperte nel legame proteina-ligando e curiose dinamiche legate alla scoperta molecolare.
it.why_it_matters: La ricerca di Leash Bio mette in luce le sfide attuali e i limiti reali nella predizione computazionale e nel binding tra molecole, offrendo spunti critici per il settore.
it.extended_analysis:
Il podcast esplora il lavoro pionieristico e le riflessioni di Leash Bio, partendo dai loro post su Substack fino alle competizioni Kaggle. Vengono affrontati temi complessi legati al legame proteina-ligando e a come i metadati e gli autori delle molecole influenzino la comprensione scientifica. L'episodio offre uno sguardo ravvicinato sulle metodologie innovative che fondono automazione di laboratorio e calcolo ad alta velocità.

Nel contesto della scoperta di farmaci guidata dall'intelligenza artificiale, comprendere dove i modelli attuali falliscono o eccellono è fondamentale per orientare i prossimi sviluppi tecnologici. Gli ascoltatori possono esaminare criticamente lo stato dell'arte e le prospettive future della ricerca biomedica computazionale.
it.context: L'episodio si inserisce nel panorama della ricerca biomedica avanzata, dove l'integrazione tra automazione di laboratorio e calcolo intensivo rappresenta una frontiera chiave per superare i limiti tradizionali della chimica computazionale.
key_takeaways: Esplorazione del concetto di Lab-in-the-Loop alla velocità di calcolo.
Analisi delle competizioni Kaggle e dei problemi irrisolti nel legame proteina-ligando.
Riflessioni sulle bizzarre scoperte relative all'attribuzione degli autori molecolari.

items.summary: For more than a decade, AI has advanced by training ever-larger models on ever-larger datasets. But as high-quality training data becomes harder to find and pretraining grows increasingly expensive, researchers are looking for new ways to keep foundation models improving. In this episode, Damian Borth, professor of AI and machine learning at the University of St. Gallen, argues we’ve been overlooking an important source of knowledge: the models we’ve already trained. His group’s work on weight space learning treats trained neural networks themselves as data, learning from the distilled results of millions of GPU hours of optimization rather than starting from raw data each time. We explore what it means to build foundation models of neural networks, how knowledge can be transferred across architectures and domains, why this approach could dramatically reduce the cost of developing specialized models, and whether future AI systems may be trained on collections of existing models instead of ever-growing datasets. 🗒️ Full show notes: https://twimlai.com/go/772.
